title: Down East Spring Birding Festival
description:
Come birding "Way Down East" over Memorial Day Weekend to Maine's Cobscook Bay Area - "one of the important bird areas in the US". Our great variety of habitats are home to many bird species.

Bird in Moosehorn National Wildlife Refuge, Roosevelt Campobello International Park, Shackford Head and Quoddy Head State Parks, and other wildlife areas.

See two dozen warblers in their breeding plumage, boreal species, and Atlantic Puffins up close and (almost) touchable. Participants find over 150 different birds each year. How many will you find?

Hikes, boat trips, presentations for advanced, intermediate, and beginning birders. Your general registration fee covers most events; some events are extra charge.

The Observatory is the tallest bridge Observatory open to the public in the entire world.

The Fort Knox state historic site is one of the best preserved examples of 19th century seacoast fortifications in the United States. Children and adults, love exploring the dark, twisting tunnels of the massive granite fortification. Visitors can easily spend several hours enjoying both attractions at this location.

title: Portraits & Voices: Shoemaking Skills of Generations
fees: $5.00 adults; $4.00 seniors and students 6 and up; Free - children 5 and under accompanied by an adult.
description: Museum L-A's third exhibit in the acclaimed Portraits & Voices series focuses on the local shoemaking industry with exhibits and activities for the whole family. Oral histories and portraits richly explore the stories of the people who helped put Auburn "on the map" as one of the largest producers of shoes in the nation at one time. These people built an industry that continues to produce world-famous shoes today. A timeline begins in the year 1824 and documents the history of shoemaking in the Twin Cities. Through photos and text learn the steps of making a shoe, welt-boot making, and about the "cottage industry" of shoemaking at home. Videos show the shoemaking process and techniques of handsewing a shoe.

description: Join Sean Fleming and his 8-piece Dam' Rag Scotta Orchestra for the "Real Ragtime Concert," a collection of classic, early 20th century Rag tunes, on Saturday, June 25, 2011 at 7:30 pm. The concert will feature compositions by Confrey, Hayden, Joplin, Lamb, Morton, Scott, and Shepherd. Included will be several works from the "Red Back Book," a collection of Ragtime orchestral arrangements published in the early 1900s. Upbeat favorites such as Joplin's "The Entertainer," "Maple Leaf Rag," and "The Easy Winners" will be mixed with slower pieces such as Lamb's "Ragtime Nightingale" and Joplin's "Solace." The piano solo "Jelly Roll Blues," an early jazz piece, will be played, well as the novelty piano piece "Dizzy Fingers."

Western Mountain Trash Can Band. Fireworks finale.

At the Festival of the Arts (10 to 4), fine artists and artisans sell and display their work. Live local music all day.

Festive, family friendly. Picnics OK, food vendors on site. Low-back chairs and blankets welcome. Evenings can be cool: sweaters are good. Sorry, no dogs, fires or candles. In extreme weather we'll move to nearby indoor venue. See website for details.

title: The Bar Harbor Mussel and Wine Festival
description:
The Bar Harbor Mussel and Wine Festival raises money for Angel Flight NE, a non-profit that flies those in need to medical care. Come enjoy local wines, mussels, and other dishes prepared by local restaurants, listen to live music, and support a great cause! For more information about the event call 207.288.2337 or visit www.atlanticbrewing.com or www.barharborcellars.com.

For more information about Angel Flight NE: http://www.angelflightne.org/

title: TWO: High Energy Juggling at the Maine Wildlife Park
description: Combining skills in juggling, contortion, acrobatics & choreography, Maine natives & brothers Matthew & Jason demonstrate team work, creativity, goal-setting, perseverance & patience. They teach children the importance of setting goals & to reach for the stars! TWO has amazed audiences across the country; & has been described as "juggling meets the X-Games!" www.twoshow.com Sponsored by: US & Co. Computers and Gray Physical Therapy

title: PORTopera's Young Artists
description:
Opera to be announced. Pre-concert talk at 1 pm.

The Young Artists program was designed to give young singers on the verge of careers an opportunity to be in a main stage production with PORTopera and to perform in a separate traveling company in smaller opera productions given within the state of Maine.

title: All About Owls Night Visit with the Live Owls of Chewonki at the Maine Wildlife Park
description: Join the owls & educators of Chewonki for a great night-time owling opportunity. Several live owls will be the stars of 2 short education programs; while the park's 4 owl species can be viewed in their normal habitats. Other 'owly' exhibits & displays will be set up around the park. 7:30-9:30pm Regular admission fees. (Call office FMI 657-4977 if raining) The Nature Store & Snack Shack will be open for snacks & souvenirs! www.chewonki.org

title: 64th Annual Riverdriver's Supper
description: 64 Annual supper at Ludden's Field. Bean-hole beans, reflector oven biscuits, potato salad, hot dogs, coleslaw, coffee, punch and sweets. Meet old friends along the Penobscot River and make new ones too! This annual event is hosted by the First Congregational Church. Come one, come all! Tickets are for sale at the field for just $7.00 per plate and kids under 12 are just $3.00. In case of inclement weather, supper may be moved to the church. See why this great event is the kickoff to the Lincoln Homecoming Festival year after year - surely a time not to be missed!

title: Tastefully Maine - Midsummer Food & Spirits in the Gardens
description: This gala party is a festive way to sample premier food and drink by many of Maine's finest chefs, caterers, and producers of food and beverages. Live music and the gorgeous surroundings at Coastal Maine Botanical Gardens make the evening even more special. This event kicks off the weekend-long Midsummer Market in the Gardens - A Gathering of Sustainable Choices. The Presenting Sponsor is the Kinckerbocker Group; the Media sponsor is Maine magazine.

title: Ogunquit Rotary Club 37th Annual 2-Cent Sale
description: A fun time for all at this unusual sale and auction.

title: Maine Lobster Ride and Roll
venueName: Oceanside High School (formerly Rockland High School)
description: The 10th Annual Maine Lobster Ride and Roll winds along country roads past swimming ponds and offers stunning views of the Maine coast. A freshly made lobster roll will be awaiting you at the ride's end. (Tuna and veggie options are available.) This fully supported ride includes four distance options: 16, 30, 50 or 100 miles. Save money by preregistering at www.BikeMaine.org. The Maine Lobster Ride & Roll supports the Bicycle Coalition of Maine's work to improve bicycling in Maine.

title: ATV Maine at the Maine Wildlife Park
description: ATV Maine was organized to promote the safe & responsible use of ATVs,towork on landowner relations & to be a unified voice on legislative issues regarding ATVs.Maine has been rated #1 nationally for its ATV trail system; & ATV Maine is a clearing house of information from local clubs statewide. Check out their exhibit, some ATVs, & find out how you can become a member of a local club. www.atvmaine.org

title: Crafts Demonstration: Lamb to Loom
description: NEW! SPECIAL! Subtitled "The Story of Wool at Shaker Village." Come enjoy this day long marathon conducted by Sandy Dzyak, a new member of our team of craftspeople. What is the day going to be-follow along from shearing, skirting, scouring to washing to carding to spinning to dyeing to weaving!

title: Trails End and Avian Taxidermy
description: Taxidermy is a method of reproducing a life-like, 3-dimensional rendition of a mammal, bird or fish for permanent display. Come & see a variety of examples of this delicate art with local taxidermists Dana Soucier & Tom Berube representing the Maine Association of Taxidermists. Dana will demonstrate the process of mounting a mammal & Tom will demonstrate how to mount waterfowl, both from start to finish. www.trailsendtaxidermystudio.com

title: 2011 BAR HARBOR MUSIC FESTIVAL
description:
The Bar Harbor Music Festival, now in its 45th year, presents recitals, opera, string orchestra, tea, pops, jazz, and "new composers" concerts throughout the month of July. Venues include a beautiful and acoustically excellent New England church, Blackwoods Campground Amphitheatre, the elegant Balance Rock Inn by the ocean,and the historic Criterion Theatre and Bar Harbor Club. The Festival's guiding purpose is to provide performance opportunities for up-and-coming artists by giving them the international stage that Bar Harbor affords.

Its annual summer festival in Bar Harbor, Maine, coupled with its Touring Program and admission-free outdoor concerts in Acadia National Park, has brought the joy of music to millions of people.

title: The Final Charge
description: A massive, museum quality display showing two huge Bull Moose with locked antlers, created by taxidermist Mark Dufresne of Nature's Reflections Taxidermy in Gray. Most often exhibited at L.L. Bean's flagship store in Freeport, this amazing display is on loan to us for our visitors to view and photograph up close! www.llbean.com

title: 4th of July Blueberry Pancake & Sausage Breakfast
description: 20th Annual breakfast will be celebrated by serving FREE meals to "active-duty military personnel". Local parade down Main Street follows at l0 am

title: Chainsaw Wildlife Artists at the Maine Wildlife Park
description: Join Maine Custom Wood Sculpture's Bill Fournier as he uses a chain saw to create eagles, bears & more. Watch a block of wood become a work of art. Also see Ron Carlson whose lifelong chainsaw carving hobby became a business; now thousands of pieces later, Ron specializes in carving bears & will have a variety of carvings on exhibit & for sale. Bring your cameras & your earplugs!

title: Maine Home + DESIGN Garden Tour: Hidden Gardens of Cape Elizabeth
description: The Hidden Gardens of Cape Elizabeth, a garden tour to benefit the Arboretum at Fort Williams, will take place on Saturday, July 9, 2011 (rain date will be July 10) from 9:00am - 3:00pm. The ten unique gardens on the tour will include an historical estate, a distinctive small farm, a Japanese-style garden, seaside gardens, a garden showcasing North American native plants, perennial gardens, a woodland garden, a native wetland garden, a cottage garden and several other exceptional gardens.

title: We Will Sustain The Structure: The Built and Natural Environments of the Shakers
description: A three day conference to be held at the Sabbathday Lake Shaker Village. Speakers, special actvities and special programs will present issues and ideas related to the Shaker experience as seen in both their built environment and the Shakers relationship to the nature that surrounds them. Covers many areas of interest! Open to all! Free conference flyer available on request!

title: 31st Camden-Rockport Antiques Show & Sale
fees: Adult Admission $6.00, $5.00 with the ad in local papers or a print out of this page. Admission is good for both days - get a Pass To Return when leaving the antiques show.
description: The 31st annual Camden-Rockport Antiques Show and Sale, sponsored by the C-R Historical Society, will be held on Saturday and Sunday, July 23 & 24, at the Camden Hills Regional High School. The Camden Show has been the premier antiques show in Maine for early 18th and 19th century furniture, Americana, and accessories. There are displays of American painted and period furniture antique & estate jewelry, antique silver, marine antiques, decoys, sporting antiques, fine glass & china including Staffordshire, Flow Blue, quimper, early soft paste; Americana, and early hearth equipment; Sandwich & other fine glass; pottery, brass, copper, and pewter; quilts and other textiles; antiquarian books, prints and paintings; and other fine antiques.

title: 55th Annual Boothbay Harbor Antiques Show & Sale
street: 261 Townsend Ave Directly on Route 27 coming into
fees: Adult Admission $6.00, with a printout of this listing $5.00 each. Children free when accompanied by an adult
description: A small but fine antiques show & sale featuring 30 dealers showing 18th and 19th century furniture, Americana, antique & estate jewelry, antique silver, decoys, sporting antiques, fine glass & china including Staffordshire, Flow Blue, quimper, early soft paste; Americana, and early hearth equipment; Sandwich & other fine glass; pottery, brass, copper, and pewter; quilts and other textiles; antiquarian books, prints and paintings; and other fine antiques. The show has been running for 54 years and is an annual event that visitors and local residents look forward to. Held at the Boothbay Region YMCA, the YMCA also hosts a silent auction to raise money for its activities. Lunch & snacks are available.

title: Searsport Lobster Boat Races and Antique Power Day
venueName: Penobscot Marine Museum, Mosman Park, and Town Dock
description: A town-wide day of activities: Lobsterboat races, antique engine and lobsterboat exhibit, radio-control model racing, crafts for children, rowing race and more.

title: Cooking With Garden Herbs
description: Here is where you'll learn, hands on, how to use many fresh herbs. When to harvest, how to dry, useful recipes for everyday meals. Samples of prepared foods, receive recipes and make herbal blends. Betsey-Ann Golon, Shaker Village herbalist, is the instructor.

title: Civil War Cannon Firing at Fort Knox

description: The 6th Maine Battery brings a full sized rifled Parrot cannon to Fort Knox for firing demonstrations. This cannon is the real deal and will provide explosive excitement for those in attendance.

title: Black Fly Follies
description:
Our popular variety show returns as members of our summer company bring their many amazing talents to Cumston stage. A great mix of comedy, music and dance. Join the party and laugh the night away with us! Rated FUN for everyone.

Tickets: $24/Adults, $22/Senior Citizens, $20/Students. Order tickets at: www.theateratmonmouth.org or call 207-933-9999 today!

title: Tommyknockers and More Bus Tour
fees: Tickets must be secured in advance - $20 per person
description:
Yankee's 2010 "Best of New England - Editor's Choice" Tour of Stephen King-dom

Join our tour guide as he takes you through the sites and sounds of Stephen King's Bangor. Visit the places that inspired King's books and movies.

title: Maine Festival of American Music
fees: $25.00 per evening concert;seniors-$20.; under 21-free. RESERVATIONS REQUIRED-(207) 926-4597
description: "America's Musics: A Rich Tapestry for the 21st Century" Sixth Season. The festival will present its most varied and eclectic program yet-Caribbean folk, contemporary composers, Shaker hymns, fusion, jazz and classical. Three evening concerts feature the Portland String Quartet, Island Beats Steel Band, the Shaker Community, violinist/fusion artist Matt Szemela. Also a one day Chamber Music Workshop and Master Class.

title: Knit A Bunny
fees: $30.00-materials included; bring own equipment as listed above
description: Knit a crouching bunny with floppy ears. Beginning knitters can do it. Participants will sew the bunny together and stuff it for a delightful, cuddly result. Pattern provided along with yarn and stuffing. Bring scissors, a yarn needle, crochet hooks-H,I and J as the yarns may differ in thickness.

title: Scottish Tattoo Bagpipe Performance Bands
fees: $10 for adults and $5 for children age 10 and under
description: Fort Knox State historic site will host the annual Scottish Tattoo, this July. Four marching bagpipe bands will perform on the Fort Knox parade grounds. This popular cultural event is a hit with both children and adults. People attending this event should plan to bring a blanket or chair, sit on and perhaps a picnic.

title: Breach of Promise - The Pollard Breckinridge Affair
description: Maine historian and author Elizabeth DeWolfe talks about her latest book, a work-in-progress about one of the biggest political and sex scandals of the late nineteenth century, the Madeline Pollard vs. Congressman William C.P. Breckinridge breach of promise case. The 1894 trial and verdict involved the most controversial issues of the time - sexual mores, gender biases, women's suffrage and the question of the character of American politicians. A young Jennie Tucker played a small and surprising role in this story, far from her home at Castle Tucker in Wiscasset.

title: Boothbay In Bloom Fashion Show & Cocktail Party
description: A silent auction and fashion show of beautiful clothing and accessories for men, women and children. View the year's most smashing fashions in the Harbor, modeled by some dashing figures to a dynamic musical score while enjoying an assortment of delicious hors d'oeuvres on the waterfront. Fisherman's Wharf Inn. Tickets sold in advance.

title: Pirate Day at Fort Knox
fees: Regular Fort admission and a $3 event donation.
description: Join the professional Pirates of the Dark Rose for a day of swashbuckling sword fights, duels, cannon fire and pirate ship attack. The pirate ship "Must Roos" will let loose cannon fire on the Fort as she sails the waters of the Penobscot River, in search of booty. The festival will feature a treasure hunt, pirate parade (all are encouraged to attend dressed in your best pirate attire), best dressed and most authentic sounding pirate contests. Regular Fort admission and a $3 per person event donation requested, because pirates love their gold!

title: Bar Harbor Garden Club's Tour of Island Gardens
description: Tour 7 beautiful Island Gardens on July 17, rain or shine from 10-4. $25 day of tour and $20 before July 17. Check out www.barharborgardenclub.com for more information.

title: Twilight Tours at the Nickels-Sortwell House
description: Come and enjoy a special early evening tour of this beautiful mansion. Built in 1807 for Captain William Nickels, this high Federal style house is a testament to Wiscasset's heyday as a seaport. Purchased by the Sortwell family in 1899, the house was lovingly restored and decorated in the Colonial Revival style. See rooms not usually open to the public, offering a deeper picture of how the Sortwell family and their servants lived in the house in the summer. Pre-registration is required for ticket purchase. Tours are at 5:00 and 6:00.

title: Paranormal/Psychic Faire
fees: Admission Fees Fort Knox $3 Adults $1 Children 5 - 11 Children under 5 are free! * $2 event donation requested to cover event costs
description: The annual Paranormal/Psychic Faire at Fort Knox presents an opportunity for visitors to learn about ghost hunting, UFOs, cryptozoology, dowsing and meet with psychics. Loren Coleman, who has appeared on the History Channel, will update his research on undocumented animals such as bigfoot and sea serpents.

title: Beginner's Woodcarving
fees: $25.00. Add $18.00 if you want to buy a carving knife.
description: Start a new hobby. Learn the basics of carving and go home with a finished carving of a Scottie dog. Participants will learn the proper use of the knife including the types of cuts and how to sharpen the knife. Norm Devonshire, a master carver, is the instructor.

title: Shaker Style Bench
fees: $40.00. Please make note of the special tools that you must bring.
description: Make a 14" high pine bench of Shaker design that can also be used as a small side table. Learn how to create a series of interlocking, wedged mortise and tenon joints. Bench will be completed during the workshop but participants will add their own finish at home. NOTE: Please bring a square, knife, marking gauge,saw, chisel and mallet. Chris Becksvoort, author of "The Shaker Legacy," is a well known craftsman, teacher and writer.

title: Maine Farm Day
description: Shaker Village opens at 12 NOON as a part of this state wide celebration of Maine agriculture. Enjoy wagon rides and barn tours, sheep and Scottish Highland cattle, the Shaker Store, barbecued food, Museum Reception Center with gifts and exhibits, tours of our Herb Department and gardens, and our new architecture exhibit.

title: Nooks and Crannies Tour of Castle Tucker
fees: $10 members. $15 nonmembers. Pregistration for ticket purchase is required.
description: Join Site Manager, Peggy Konitzky on a tour that peeks into unexpected corners of this unique house. Built in 1807 and occupied by the same family for almost a hundred and fifty years, this Regency-style mansion is filled with the furnishings and belongings of the Tucker family who lived here from 1857-2003. The Tuckers were at the pinnacle of Wiscasset society for four generations but the public never saw the private turmoil of these lively and colorful personalities. Enjoy a leisurely, in-depth experience of the house with stories and rooms not included on the general tour. See where family, friends and servants stayed during the busy summers of the boarding house period.

title: Saltwater Celtic Music Festival
description: Saltwater, one of the premier Celtic music events in New England, is held at beautiful Thomas Point Beach and Campground in Brunswick. Highlights include a diverse roster of internationally renowned musicians, sand beach, playground, manicured grounds and Celtic-themed vendors. Saltwater satellite events occur at leading Maine venues (Maine Irish Heritage Center, Maine Maritime Museum, Skye Theatre, Unity Centre, Byrnes' Irish Pubs ) on the days leading up to Saltwater.

title: Red Cloak Haunted History Tours
description: Lantern-lit walking tours of intown areas with the Lady in the Red Cloak; Camden, Damariscotta, Bath, Wiscasset, Boothbay Harbor. Come with us as we find ghosts and history, spirits and mystery! $10 adults, $7 under 12, free under 5. Call or e-mail for reservations. See calendar at www.redcloakhauntedhistorytours.com

title: The Moxie Festival
description:
Since 1983, The Moxie Festival Weekend in Lisbon, Maine has been held on the second weekend in July.

The Festival now includes a three day Pow Wow; Friday night fireworks show; a Saturday parade, 5K race, and family fun carnival; and on Sunday, the Chief Worumbo Androscoggin River Race. Moxie was designated Maine's official soft drink on May 20, 2005.

Learn traditional canoeing and camping skills at historic Camp Winona. Land and water workshops. Event goes on rain or shine! Classes for all levels of canoeists are one and a quarter hours long, enabling participants to enjoy a range of activities. Equipment is provided. Children's paddling and campcraft program also. This is a great weekend event for the whole family.

Most people come for the weekend and camp, either with their own tent or trailer or stay in Winona's large wall tents.

Day registration available.

Registration forms available on our website.

description: 'BRI' is a leader in creative, interactive education & works to personalize wildlife issues among students, educators, scientists & the public. By harnessing the power of state-of-the-art technology, people are connected to wildlife & ecological science through the use of BRI webcams, with 24hr live-streaming video of nesting eagles, loons, osprey & peregrine falcons. www.briloon.org

One of the largest family musical events in New England, the Blistered Fingers Bluegrass Festival takes place Thurs - Sunday in June and August. This Event attracts thousands of music lovers from all over the world to hear some of the Greatest Bluegrass music. With banjos, fiddles, and those high, lonesome harmonies converging in Litchfield twice a year, this event features many national and local bands. Come Experience the "Welcome Home" feeling. description: Maine's northern most birding event, in Presque Isle, is open to everyone who would like to learn more about birding. This birding festival offers guided bird walks, birding activities which include bird banding, calling and carving demonstrations, live bird displays, a bird house building station and boat rides. Friendly people will create a wonderful outdoor wildlife experience at Maine's First State Park. The wooded hiking trails and lake shoreline offers attractive bird habitat, where over 100 different bird species have been seen, a great opportunity to increase ones life list. FMI call the park at 207-768-8341 or go to www.parksandlands.com. Camping is available, to make reservations go to www.CAMPWITHME.com .

Learn how to identify the different types of ticks found in Maine, & get tips on prevention & basic information on the disease itself. What do Asian Long horned Beetles look like? Be on the lookout - they attack & kill healthy hardwood trees & a huge effort is being made to keep them OUT of Maine! www.mmcri.org/lyme/meticks www.albmaine.org

We offer field trips, pelagic trips, paddling adventures, workshops, social gatherings, and evening presentations. By land or by sea, we'll find some exciting birds for you to see.

title: High Federal - The Architecture of the Nickels-Sortwell House
fees: Free for Historic New England Members. $15 nonmembers.
description: Come hear Earle Shettleworth, director of the Maine Historic Preservation Commission and Maine State Historian, share his insights into the architecture and building of one Maine's most elegant mansions. The Nickels-Sortwell House is the finest example of high Federal style architecture north of Portsmouth. Captain William Nickels, a wealthy sea captain, built the house in 1807 as a statement of his success at the peak of Wiscasset's prosperity. Run as an inn after his death for many years under multiple owners, the house was lovingly restored in the Colonial Revival style by the Sortwell family of Cambridge, MA after they purchased it in 1899. This is a Historic New England Members' Month program, specially open to the public.

description: Big house, little house, back house, barn - the 1789 Marrett House is one of the best examples of this traditional New England rural architectural configuration. This class requires the use of knives and gouges so bring your tools with you. A blank will be provided. Norm will be available on August 6, from 9 - noon for those who need more guidance.

title: Guided Walking Tour of Historic Downtown Presque Isle
description: A FREE guided walking tour of historic downtown Presque Isle, Maine covering two miles and taking approximately two hours. Tour starts and ends at the Vera Estey House at 16 Third Street, Presque Isle. On street parking available.

title: Natalie Stovall concert to be held at UMPI
description:
The University of Maine at Presque Isle will host fiddle-playing singer Natalie Stovall at 8 p.m. on May 7 in Wieden Gymnasium. Since her first professional gig singing and playing the fiddle at the age of 10, Natalie has performed everywhere from Oprah to the Grand Ole Opry. She was the first performer ever to be invited to sing God Bless America for the President at the White House Press Correspondents Dinner. She has also performed at colleges all over the United States and now she will be bringing her talents to UMPI for a night of great entertainment.

One free ticket to this concert will be available for UMPI, NMCC, and SAGE students and must be picked up in advance.

title: Thomaston Place Auction Galleries' Spring Fine Art, Antiques & Jewelry Auction
description: On May 21 & 22, 2011, Thomaston Place Auction Galleries will present 1200 lots of Fine American and European Art; Chinese, Japanese & Russian treasures; early silver; antique furniture; oriental carpets; rare books & ephemera, plus fine estate jewelry, gold coins and watches. Auction begins at 11:00 a.m. each day. Previews: May 16 - 20, 9:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m.; and 9:00 - 11:00 a.m. each auction day. Auction participants may register for live, absentee, telephone, or internet bidding. Visit www.thomastonauction.com for further details.

title: Plow Day
fees: Free admission; donations gratefully accepted. $5 pony rides. Refreshments for sale.
description: Draft horses will plow and harrow several acres of farmland in a free demonstration put on by Skyline Farm, Deri Farm (located next door), and the Farmers Draft Horse, Mule and Pony Club of Maine. The teams will begin at 9 a.m. and finish around 2 p.m. (rain date May 14) A wagon will shuttle spectators between Skyline Farm and the fields at Deri Farm, which will serve as the demonstration area. Skyline Farm Carriage Museum will be exhibiting horse-drawn summer delivery vehicles. Blacksmith Tim Greene of Parsonsfield will forge objects out of metal using Skyline Farm's antique forge. In the Skyline arena, pony and horse rides will be available at $5 each. Food for sale. Parking is available at Skyline and along the roadside where permitted.

title: Taste of Bar Harbor Merchant Street Stroll and Craft Fair
description:
The Bar Harbor Merchant Street and Craft Fair is an annual event to highlight Bar Harbor merchants and local crafters. Bar Harbor merchants all have something unique to offer. On May 21st, stroll the streets to get a Taste of what it is that makes them special.

It will be a true Sidewalk Sale! Additionally we will be hosting a Taste of Bar Harbor Craft Fair, located in the parking lot adjacent to The First. Come support your local favorites and discover some new ones along the way.

Each year the Bar Harbor Merchants Association donates the proceeds from table registration to an Island Non-Profit. This year's recipient is The Common Good Caf~ Soup Kitchen located in Southwest Harbor.

title: New Surry Theatre Presents: An Evening With ee cummings
venueName: The Blue Hill Town Hall Theater
description: New Surry Theatre actor Jeffrey Brink will perform a dramatic presentation of some of e e cummings poetry. One of America's most popular and best-loved poets, cummings' poetry can be hard to read due to his interesting use of form, syntax, punctuation and language. All this changes when performed dramatically: it comes alive. More information at www.newsurrytheatre.org

title: Mechanic Falls Community Day
description:
Planning is well underway for the 2nd Annual Community Day. This year's event will be slightly expanded to include some activity on Friday evening June 24th. A full day of events will be on Saturday, June 25th in throughout the downtown area.

Building on last year's success, several of the events will be returning and new ones have been planned. Confirmed events are the annual Pottle Hill Road Race, the American Legion Chicken BBQ, The Library's book sale, the Horribles parade, along with many other exhibitors, vendors and games.

It is sure to be a fun filled day for the whole family.

Information and applications are available on line at www.sacospirit.com, e-mail sacospirit@hotmail.com, call 207-286-3546.

Come celebrate...our agricultural roots, past traditions, the way we live today, old fashioned and country cuisine, bluegrass music, and our community.

The farm fest promotes agricultural and rural living and offers many hands-on activities and horse farming demonstrations. Folks can also enjoy bluegrass music, experience unique purchasing opportunites, and sample delicious country cuisine while visiting with friends and family.
time: 10 to 5 on June 25 and 10 to 4 on June 26

title: 30th Anniversary Summer Concert Series
fees: FREE! Bring your own lawn chair on which to sit.
description: The 45-member Auburn Community Concert Band is celebrating its 30th anniversary performance season. Since 1982, the band has been presenting free weekly concerts in downtown Auburn throughout each summer. A different musical theme is presented EVERY WEDNESDAY EVENING. Selections range from Big Band songs to present day hits ... from Broadway Show tunes to favorite patriotic medlies. Ample free parking is available in the parking garage located across the street from the plaza. In case of inclement weather, performances take place inside the Hilton Garden Inn Auburn Riverwatch, located one block North at Great Falls Plaza.

title: 2011 Saco Spirit Main Street Car Show
fees: $5 registration for cars Free to the public
description: 2nd Annual Saco Spirit Main St Car Show will be presented in downtown Saco, Maine on July 30th. The show features nine catagories of antique and specialty cars along with vendors, displays, demonstrations, music, food and fun. Registation begins at 8am and the first place trophies in all nine catagories will be awarded at 2pm on the music stage on Main Street. There will be a 50/50 raffle and show merchandise for sale. We anticipate over one hundred car entries this year so come on down and have some fun!

title: Pedal to the Port
fees: Registration is $30 for a team member; $35 for an individual. Free T-shirt and cookout included! Proceeds benefit Trekkers' youth mentoring programs.
description: Trekkers' Pedal to the Port is an annual fundraising bike ride that starts in the historic town of Thomaston. Bikers travel down the picturesque St. George peninsula to Port Clyde and back. This is a fun and casual ride for all ages, with 3 routes to choose from: 12, 35 and 47 miles. Registration is $30 for a team member; $35 for an individual. Free T-shirt and cookout included! Proceeds benefit Trekkers' youth mentoring programs. Join us for this beautiful coastal ride. We hope to see you there!

title: Close to The Coast 5k & 10K
fees: $15 Registration for the race, which includes a possible t-shirt. All activities for the Winslow Park Family Fun Day are free, including food and admittance to the park for the day.
description:
This year the race marks its 16th Anniversary! The course is run on quiet roads and forest trails along the ocean in beautiful Winslow Park, the home of the Lobsterman Triathlon. Registration is from 7:15 am to 8:45 am with the race starting at 9:00 am.

The Race is part of the Winslow Park Family Fun Day, a great time for families with all the events free of charge. Enjoy free entrance to the park for the day, hotdogs, ice cream, games, swimming, activities, playground and a moon bounce house. Oceanside camping is available for those wanting to stay over night.

Registration is $15.00 with guaranteed t-shirt through June 10, 2010 and $15.00 with possible t-shirt through race day. We pride ourselves on our race prizes, PIES! The top 2 finishers in each category receive a pie! Additionally, there will be a 1K Kids Fun Run after the main race which requires no application or fees and children's prizes provided by Wilbur's of Maine.

Race proceeds support the Freeport Rotary Club Scholarship program and other local charitable projects.

Visit www.freeport-rotary.org for more information.

title: Seacoast Water Garden Club 2011 Tour
description:
Think Spring! Or better yet, Summer! The Seacoast Water Garden Club is hosting its sixth annual pond tour this summer! The tour will run on consecutive Sundays from mid-June through mid August with the exception of July 3. Each Sunday from 12 Noon until 4PM, one or two ponds are open for public viewing. We anticipate a wonderful collection of water gardens this year, ranging from small backyard sanctuaries to a large property with 13 ponds! Each garden offers a unique example of how a water garden can be created to fit almost any situation.

The Club is comprised simply of area people who, as Booker Nevius from the Water Garden Department at Wentworth Greenhouses says, "Love their pond or would love to have a pond"! In 2006, Kare

description: Family Fun Day is a non-profit event meant to encourage and support the numerous community, school groups and non-profit organizations in our town by providing them a venue to raise much needed revenue while encouraging the small town spirit of caring and community that is New England. The day kicks off with a parade at 10:30 AM which starting from Cottage Farm Road. There will be floats from local community groups and sports teams, as well as antique cars, bands, lots of fire engines from many of the local towns, and much more. Activities are scheduled throughout the day including games for all ages, face painting, numerous arts and crafts and a wide variety of foods and beverages.

title: Marty Stuart and his Fabulous Superlatives
description: Since starting out singing gospel as a child, a bluegrass stint with Lester Flatt in the '70s, six years with Johnny Cash in the '80s, and coming up with his smash 'hillbilly rock' hits of the '90s, the five time GRAMMY-winner, platinum recording artist, and leader of the extraordinary touring and recording band The Fabulous Superlatives, Marty Stuart steadily continues to preserve the roots, culture and history of traditional country music. Without question, Marty has evolved into one of the most important roots musicians in America today, as well as one of country music~s best performers. A don~t miss show! Tickets $35/General Admission

description:
A Benefit Celebration of Maine Made Music (and Beyond)

A day long Music festival with over 20 Original Bands and Musicians from Maine and beyond. Proceeds of the event are donated to local charities and organizations in need. We have 2 stages of music, a kids area, food and art vending. Original music from Folk and Bluegrass to Indie rock and country. Music begins at 11:00am and goes all day until 8:00pm. title: Classical Concert with Felix Hell
fees: $15, 2 for $25, 13-21, $5, under 12 free Tickets available through PortTix, 207-842-0800, porttix.com Groups of 20+ get a 10% discount Rush tickets (suggested $10-15) go on sale at 7:00 pm
description: Felix has recorded six CDs, critically acclaimed by the public as well as by experts. His music has been broadcast by PIPEDREAMS, as well as by radio stations of Germany, The Netherlands, Australia, and by the BBC in Great Britain. Orchestra performances comprise concerts with the Charleston Symphony Orchestra, USA, the National Academy Orchestra of Canada under Boris Brott, and the NEC Philharmony, Boston, USA, under Jens Georg Bachmann.
time: "Kotzschmar Konversations", pre-concert chats 6:30-7. Show begins at 7:30 PM

title: Camille A. Brown & Dancers
description: The vivid and versatile Camille A. Brown is a pixy-ish performer who packs a punch. Brown's passionate dances tell stories of historical moments and ordinary lives using a mixture of contemporary dance and African dance styles. Every work by Brown sends a potent message of empowerment that reverberates from the stage. For their Maine debut, Brown & Dancers offer four works including "The Groove to Nobody's Business." Originally commissioned by Ailey, "Groove" reveals humorous glimpses of humanity through Brown's bold, quicksilver dancing that is charming to the max. Also on the program are "City of Rain," "New Second Line" and a heart-stopping new solo by Brown. (Family friendly, appropriate for all ages.)

title: Maine Pro Musica
description: As part of their new summer tour, Maine Pro Musica Orchestra, under the direction of conductor Janna Hymes, will perform a special program featuring Vivaldi~s Four Seasons, coupled with the fiery music of Argentinian tango composer Astor Piazzolla~s Four Seasons based on the original. Violin virtuoso, Irina Muresanu, will be the featured guest artist in these performances. Music by Tchaikovsky and Puccini will round out this exciting program. Tickets $25/General Admission

description: Leichter and ultra-glam-fab singer-songwriter Monstah Black reimagine New York's underground through extravagant song and dance, decorated with club, video, funk, hip-hop, fashion and drag. (Village Voice) (Contains mature themes and explicit language.)

title: Zoe | Juniper
description: Two time National Dance Project award winners, Zoe | Juniper construct three-dimensional art that melds precise dance performance with evocative video and photographic techniques, juxtaposing restrained wildness and delicate fury. Zoe | Juniper return to Bates with "A Crack in Everything", a multi-disciplinary performance combining Scofield's disciplined physical distortion of classical technique with Shuey's distilled visual design. "A Crack..." employs the Greek Tragedy "The Oresteia" as a lens to understand the emotional spectrum of justice and retaliation. (Adult content)
